note: The AGENTS.md hard rules as data (issue #53), seeded from AGENTS.md, the privilege map and eMMC layout in findings 04/07, and HANDOFF-2026-11-09-LANE3. Every match is a refusal, never a warning; check() applies rules in listed order and returns the first hit. The stock bundle itself (/APPS/.../app.js) is deliberately NOT listed: replacing it is the installer's whole job, gated structurally — bootstrap pins the stock md5/sha256 and takes the once-only backup before any write. The selfTest block arms the typo guard: every rule must catch the paths listed under its own id, every allowed path must pass, and a rule that matches nothing in the list is an error at require time.

rules.reason: Creating this file starts the root factory-reset flow at the next boot; /var/tvservice is writable for us, which is exactly why it must stay free of triggers (findings 04).

start-hisense.sh consumes this marker at every boot and runs set_ipk_path.sh as root for each directory it lists — that is the documented root-exec lane, not a product action; the launcher installs nothing through IPK (findings 04).

The true pre-native watcher config, left by the 2026-11-09 manual session (HANDOFF-2026-11-09-LANE3, 'The one thing to know'); native-install seeds the rollback backup from it, so overwriting it loses the only copy of the canvas-launcher setup.

The watcher config as it was before the first CLI-managed native install; rollback restores it byte-for-byte. It is taken once by cp -p on the TV and never replaced — a write here makes rollback restore the wrong config.

/OAD is writable (p42) but it is the OTA lane: otaflag=170 boots rcS.OTA/rc.ota from here and opkg stages downloads in /OAD/pkgs/download. Never write, never delete, never stage UI assets here — verified-boot assets live under /APPS/channelA, never /OAD (AGENTS.md; findings 03/04).

The UI engine's own shell (index.html, static JS). Only the operation-ui launcher module is ours; this tree is the HASHES baseline native-home verifies before every install, and a write here breaks the Home while looking like a successful install (HANDOFF-2026-11-09-LANE3; native-trial.cjs HASHES).

The root-run deploy_oem_data.sh copies this tree unfiltered into /hidata, /vendor/tvconfig/config and /serialdata at boot. Staging files here is the root OEM-deploy lane, not the launcher's (findings 04).

Read-only rootfs (dm-verity squashfs): phoenix, the engine binaries and start scripts (/opt/hisenseUI), vendor packages. Verified boot carries this partition — writes are impossible as well as forbidden (findings 04).
System partition p23, mounted ro: boot scripts source /application/network. Off the rw lane by design (findings 04/07).
System partition p26, mounted ro: daemon_profile and boot configuration. Off the rw lane by design (findings 04/07).
System partition p37, mounted ro: start-hisense.sh, deploy, the login gates. This is the root-side boot chain and stays stock (findings 04/07).
Vendor libraries and tvconfig. deploy_oem_data.sh writes here as root — that is the vendor's deployer, never ours (findings 04).
The hidata partitions: critical.ini and the factory/model data boot consumes (findings 04/07).
Raw eMMC partitions (42 on the reference unit). Dumps read them; nothing ever writes one — a write here is a firmware image bypassing the filesystem, and verified boot must stay green (findings 07).
